paragraphs.heading: A friend with a way out
paragraphs.edited: Years ago our family became friends with another young family in our neighborhood. The kids were about the same age as our kids, and the mom and dad had a lot in common with my wife and I. Well, as we got to know him, it was very clear that the father, who became a good friend of mine, was not a Christian. In fact, we had conversations about heaven and hell. We had conversations about the scientific evidence for God, and he was the consummate skeptic. He always had a way out, or a question, or a way of avoiding the evidence. And then years later they ended up moving to the Northwest.

paragraphs.edited: When I heard that they were going to move, I had a couple of thoughts. I thought, well, number one, gosh, he's no longer going to have me in his life, and other Christian friends in our neighborhood, to talk to him about God. And he's such a skeptic, he's never going to believe. But then sometime later I started noticing he was posting quotes by C.S. Lewis on social media. He was posting these Christian ideas. To make a long story short, a few summers ago I had a chance to go up to the Northwest and baptize him, because he'd become a Christian. And on that same day his young son was baptized as well. It was truly one of the most amazing experiences of my life.

paragraphs.heading: Four principles
paragraphs.edited: I think there's four principles we can learn from this experience. First, for many people, coming to faith can take a long time, sometimes even years. Many people have emotional, intellectual, moral and relational issues to work through, and this is certainly true for my friend, before they can consider the claims of Christ. Second, sometimes people are at a point in their lives where they're just not open to faith. Even people walked away from Jesus in the flesh.

paragraphs.edited: Years ago, when my friend was still a skeptic, I had him speak into a group of my high school students, and I was trying to teach my students, how do you have genuine conversations with people who see the world differently? And in the middle of this conversation, my friend said to my students, look, if your teacher Sean could give me evidence, I would believe. I just don't see the evidence. And then in the conversation later, somehow it shifted. I don't remember how, but somehow the group was talking about the legalization of marijuana, and my friend says, he goes, look, the bottom line is I just don't want the government coming into my house telling me how to live. It's my house.

paragraphs.heading: It was never the evidence
paragraphs.edited: And I stopped him. I said, wait a minute, a minute ago you said you'd follow the evidence. Now I think you have the answer why you don't. You know, Jesus says, I stand at the door and knock. He's the ultimate governing authority. God wants to come into your house and tell you how to live. You didn't want the government to tell you whether you could smoke marijuana or not. Maybe the real issue is you just don't want God in your life telling you how to live. He looked at me and he says, I don't understand. I tried three times to explain it, and I gave up. Do you know that years later, when he became a Christian, he pointed back to that, and he said, Sean, you were right. It wasn't a lack of evidence. I simply did not want an authority in my life telling me how to live. Friends, sometimes people are not at a point in their life, for a variety of reasons, to even be open to issues of faith.

paragraphs.heading: Relationships really matter
paragraphs.edited: And fourth, relationships really matter. It was certainly truth that was important in my friend's journey, but it was also the love and relationship of believers that drew him in when his heart was open. We've talked a lot in this study about how important it is to speak truth, but to do it in a loving fashion. Jesus came in grace and he came in truth. Yes, we need to speak truth, but from a heart of love and a heart of compassion. In fact, we need to be willing to love people because they're made in the image of God, even if they never come to faith.

paragraphs.heading: The journey we have taken
paragraphs.edited: We have been on a long journey together. We started by looking at the relationship between faith and reason and exploring questions of truth. Then we looked at some different worldviews: pantheism, naturalism and monotheism. Then we considered the scientific evidence from DNA and fine-tuning, pointing toward an intelligent designer. And then after that, we looked at these signposts that point toward purpose in the universe: beauty, morality, free will and story. Then we examined the specific historical evidence for Jesus and for the reliability of the Bible. And then after that we considered some of the biggest objections to the faith, hell and evil.

paragraphs.heading: You are ready
paragraphs.edited: And in this final unit we've asked the question, what now? Do you have all your questions answered? Probably not. In fact, you might even have more questions now than when we started. But I want to impress something very important upon you, and it's this: that you are ready. You've been trained well. I had a public debate some years ago, and I called up one of my professors from grad school, and as we were talking about it he said something to me I'll never forget. He said, Sean, you've been trained well. And the same is true for you. You will always have questions. There's always new issues that arise. But you have learned truth well, and you are ready, if you put your training into practice, to engage family and friends and others of our non-believing world with the gospel.

paragraphs.heading: Will that be you?
paragraphs.edited: Friends, we live in a broken and a hurting world that desperately needs Jesus. We live in a world that desperately needs people to speak the truth about Jesus, the only truth that can set people free. The question is, will that be you?
